title: Contracts that drew a single bid
question: How often does a City construction contract attract only one bidder, and what does that bid cost against the engineer’s estimate?
finding: 7 of 108 bid lists had one bidder (and 16 more had two), worth $93.9 million; the lone bid ran a median +14% against the estimate, where the low bid on contested contracts ran -7%.
how: Each published tabulation is one list; a list with one row is a single bid. The bid is compared with the engineer’s estimate printed on the same document.
limits: The sample is small: 108 bid lists (71 Public Works 2022–26, 15 Port, 22 Muni), only contracts large enough to go to a commission with the tabulation attached. The airport and the water department publish none without a login. A single bid is common for specialised work (dredging, tunnel track, fuel systems); the estimate may cover a different scope than the bid total; one row is a job-order contract bid as a mark-up factor, with no dollar figure.
